- 2026-10-13 (Lane B2): REPORT ONLY, the 401 on /api/usageDashboard?view=ops after the key rotation, and the sales-epoch behaviour. No code changed, no request made with the key for this job (code reading only).
  FOR LANE B / FOR SAM, Part 1, the credential check (read from the code, not tested):
    1. Gate: handleOps (api/usageDashboard.js ~413) calls hasServerCredential(req) from lib/_credential.js and nothing else. The 401 text "Unauthorized (ops)" is that one branch. No host check, no launch stage, no IP check, no second key, no cookie. Method must be GET or POST and the address must carry view=ops. A key in the address or body is ignored by design.
    2. Variables compared, exact names: PROBE_KEY and OPS_KEY (either one matches), and CRON_SECRET (only as `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`). USAGE_DASHBOARD_KEY / ADMIN_DASHBOARD_KEY are NOT involved: they gate the other dashboard views (x-admin-key), and the ops branch returns before that check.
    3. Headers: x-ops-key and x-probe-key are both accepted, either one. Comparison is byte-exact with crypto.timingSafeEqual and a length check. The code does NOT trim the environment value, so a trailing space, newline or quote saved into the Vercel variable can never match (Node already trims whitespace around the incoming header, so only the stored value can carry it).
    4. What the status code tells us: a 500 "Set PROBE_KEY in Vercel" is returned only when PROBE_KEY, OPS_KEY and CRON_SECRET are ALL unset in that deployment. We get 401, so at least one of the three exists in the running deployment and the sent value did not equal PROBE_KEY or OPS_KEY. The request is reaching the function (it is not Vercel's bot challenge, which would be a 429 or a challenge page).
    5. x-launch-stage-test path: lib/_launchStage.js launchStage()/launchBusinessOn() call the SAME hasServerCredential. The stage header is honoured only after that check passes; it does validate the key value, it does not just look for the header. So both paths read the same variables (PROBE_KEY / OPS_KEY / CRON_SECRET) through the same function.
    6. Why pushCheck can still pass with a rejected key (the likely answer to the contradiction): scripts/pushCheck.mjs marks a page PASS when status < 500 and there is no 5xx or console error; it does NOT assert that it stayed on /market-check or /buy. If the key is rejected, launchStage falls back to LAUNCH_STAGE and a gated page redirects to /sell, which loads fine and prints PASS. The script's own header says so ("a redirect to Sell ... still proves no 5xx"). The final URL is printed in the PASS line: a /sell there for the Market Check or Buy row means the key was NOT accepted. Lane B should read that column, and Lane C may want to make the script fail when a keyed page ends on /sell. I did not run it.
    7. Other possible causes visible from the code: the scripts send the Keychain value, so a Keychain value that differs from what Vercel holds (set before/after the rotation, or a different environment) is the simplest explanation. Vercel env changes only reach NEW deployments, so a rotated variable without a redeploy leaves the running functions on the old value.
  FOR SAM, what to check in Vercel (no key is ever shown or typed into chat):
    1. vercel.com, open the goasksam project, then Settings, then Environment Variables.
    2. Find PROBE_KEY (and OPS_KEY if it exists). Note which environments it ticks: Production must be ticked. If there are two PROBE_KEY rows (one Production, one All or Preview), delete the stale one so only one row covers Production.
    3. Click the three dots on the PROBE_KEY row, Edit. Do not reveal it. Retype nothing; paste the new key from your clipboard (copied from the Keychain item with `security find-generic-password -s goasksam-probe -w | pbcopy`) into the value box. Paste only the key: no space before or after, no newline, no quotes. Tick Production. Save.
    4. If the row says "Sensitive", the value cannot be read back; that is expected. Saving a new value replaces it.
    5. Go to Deployments, open the latest Production deployment, three dots, Redeploy (leave "use existing build cache" on or off, either works). Wait until it shows Ready. A variable change does nothing for the running deployment until this redeploy finishes.
    6. Then in Terminal run `! node scripts/pushCheck.mjs` style checks as before and read the final address column: Market Check and Buy rows should end on /market-check and /buy, not /sell.
    7. If it still returns 401 after the redeploy: check whether CRON_SECRET was the variable you rotated instead (it is only accepted as Authorization: Bearer, not in x-ops-key), and check that the Keychain item goasksam-probe holds the same value you pasted in step 3 (copy it again from the Keychain rather than from an old note).
  FOR LANE B, Part 2, lib/_epoch.js and its callers (code reading):
    1. currentEpoch(env) when the app_config sales_epoch row is missing: returns the last known value, which is null before any bump on that instance. When the read throws, or env.supabaseUrl/Key is missing, it also returns the last known value (null on a fresh instance). A blank or missing value never replaces a known one.
    2. Quirk: the 5-second poll shortcut only applies when cached.value is NOT null (`cached.value != null && ...`). With a null epoch the `at` stamp is updated but never used, so EVERY call goes to Supabase (concurrent callers share one in-flight read). A missing row therefore costs one app_config read per cache check instead of one per five seconds.
    3. Cache reads and a null epoch: rangeCache (search.js ~549), specMem reads (~912, ~1015, ~1020) all use `entry.epoch === epoch`. null === null is TRUE, so with the epoch unavailable they fall through to the version and TTL checks, not a miss. The warm-row read (~896) is looser: it misses only when BOTH the current epoch and the row's warmEpoch are truthy and different, so a row with no warmEpoch is served whatever the epoch is.
    4. Entries written before today: an in-process entry has no epoch field at all only if it was written by code that predates the epoch gate; `undefined === null` is FALSE, so such an entry is a MISS against a null epoch and against a real one. In practice in-memory Maps do not survive a deploy, so this cannot occur on current instances. The persisted spec_market_cache rows are not compared on epoch directly: specMem is restamped with the epoch current at read time (~943), and the row's own freshness is engineVersion plus its 24-hour age. The warm rows (~896) with no warmEpoch field are served, as in 3.
    5. answerCacheable (search.js ~517): null is cacheable; a tier other than result/thin/refusal is cacheable. For result/thin/refusal it REJECTS when fallbackRung is not one of exact, year_widened, generation, model_any_year, sibling, not_enough_data, when rungLabel is blank, or when the receipt count (rawPool length, else cards length) differs from poolN (thin: thin.totalN). A normal result passes today: its poolN is solid.length (onebox.js ~4255) and its rawPool is that same solid array. It can reject a normal result only if a later step replaces rawPool or cards without updating poolN (a rescue or refine that swaps the pool), or a path returns a fallbackRung outside that set. Rejection is silent: the caller still gets the answer, it just is not cached, so the symptom would be repeat loads recomputing, not wrong numbers.

  PART 1, the cache fix. Root cause confirmed by code reading: api/sellerDecision.js's MCWARM fast path read the warm cache (readWarmAnswer) but never wrote to it on a miss - only scripts/warmMarketCheck.js (the nightly curated-list job) called writeWarmAnswer. A version bump invalidates every row by design (the gate the mechanism exists for), but nothing then re-filled it except the next scheduled nightly run, so every bare-nameplate load stayed slow until someone ran task=warmMC by hand. Fixed: wantsWarm now covers every resolved spec (trim included, not only bare nameplates), and a miss writes the live answer back under the current ENGINE_VERSION before returning - one slow load per spec per version, not every load. Mileage stays excluded (obRefine, which already gates miles/gearbox/body/driver/observe refines, is excluded from wantsWarm exactly as it was before this job).
    scripts/postDeployWarm.mjs: calls task=warmMC, then loads all 20 golden cars once through the real public /market-check page (the one path that exercises the write-through fix, since task=warmMC itself only ever covers bare nameplates). Run twice this job (after e28/e29 landed, and again after e30) - both runs showed the mechanism working: every car not already warm computed once, slowly, and every later load of the identical spec was fast. Documented in this file: every lane runs scripts/postDeployWarm.mjs once after an ENGINE_VERSION bump reaches production, before trusting the speed check.
    Part 1(b) table. "Cold" = the first compute of that spec under e30 (from the second postDeployWarm run, the public page, real browser). "Warm" = five back-to-back loads of the identical spec right after, same path.
    | Car | Round | Hit/Miss | Reason | ms |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 1995 Porsche 911 Carrera | cold | miss | never warmed before this fix (a trim query) | 20740 |
    | 1995 Porsche 911 Carrera | warm 1-5 | hit | write-through row from the cold load | 5367, 3780, 2841, 3645, 3147 |
    | 2008 Porsche 997 Carrera S Coupe | cold | miss | same reason | 12306 |
    | 2008 Porsche 997 Carrera S Coupe | warm 1-5 | hit | write-through row | 3159, 2710, 4117, 2815, 5284 |
    | 1969 Chevrolet Camaro | cold-equivalent | hit | already warmed by task=warmMC (step 1 of the same run, a bare nameplate) | 6670 |
    | 1969 Chevrolet Camaro | warm 1-5 | hit | same row | 4247, 3410, 4037, 3096, 3144 |
    All ten warm reads sit at 2.7-5.4s, comfortably under PERF_WARM_MS (8000) - confirmed again by the FORMAL gate, scripts/pushCheck.mjs, run clean after all of this: "2008 Porsche 997 Carrera S Coupe" 2849ms/14000, "1995 Porsche 911 Carrera" 3358ms/14000, "1969 Chevrolet Camaro" 5641ms/18000 and 3388ms/8000 - all PASS. Five independent COLD reads per car are no longer obtainable by honest means now that the fix works: the whole point of write-through is that a spec is cold exactly once per engine version, so repeating "cold" five times would mean inventing four fake misses. Reported one real cold read per car instead of five, named plainly.

  PART 2, the 42-vs-30 drift and why the sweep missed it. Root cause confirmed via the keyed obdiag+cachecheck diagnostic and code reading: lib/live/search.js specKeyFor built its cache key from generation.code ALONE whenever a model had no HALF_GENERATIONS entry (911's 992, the common case) - no year component at all. Two different typed years inside the same generation (any two bare-911 queries from 2019-2026) therefore produced the IDENTICAL spec_market_cache row; whichever year's ladder computed first silently answered for every other year too, until the next write replaced it. "2025 Porsche 911" was already in scripts/crossProductCheck.js DEFAULT_SPECS, and count was already an EXACT-match field (not the 10%-tolerance low/high rule) - the sweep could not have caught this anyway, because checkOneSpec reads one spec at a time, at one moment, across the four lanes; it has no mechanism to ask "did two DIFFERENT specs silently share one cache row." That is a property of the key function itself, not of any single spec's own answer. Fixed: the literal year is now always part of the key, half-generation or not, plus edition/variant/wheelbase (real resolver fields that scope the pool the same way trim/body do and had the identical collision risk). Added a pure, DB-free regression guard, checkSpecKeyYearIsolation (scripts/crossProductCheck.js, wired into prePush.mjs on every push, zero DB) - five fixture pairs (the exact bug, the two new golden specs, the pre-existing half-generation case, Defender 90/110, 240Z Series 1) that assert specKeyFor never collides two different specs onto one key. This is the structural fix the sweep itself cannot be: it runs on every push, not just when someone happens to query two colliding years back to back in the same sweep run. "2024 Porsche 911 Carrera S Coupe" added to DEFAULT_SPECS alongside "2025 Porsche 911" per the brief's instruction, so both year-widened golden cars are standing cross-product regressions now, not just engine-vs-golden ones.

A REAL BUG, found only once real production photos were in the mix: the first "Sales behind this
answer" card on the live 2006 Mercedes-Benz CLK DTM page (which has a real photo; its two siblings
show "NO PHOTO") rendered its photo box at 320x240 (the photo's own 4:3 intrinsic ratio) instead of
the card shape's 320x213 (3:2) - visibly taller than its two placeholder-only siblings. Root cause:
`.ph{height:auto}` (aspect-ratio supplies the computed height once width is known) combined with
`.ph img{height:100%}` in normal flow - a percentage height does not resolve against an auto-height
parent, so the real `<img>` fell back to its own natural ratio and the auto-height parent grew to
fit it; the placeholder text (`.ph .none`) was already `position:absolute` and never had this
problem. Every local proof fixture in the prior round used `image: null` on every card, so this
never had a chance to surface locally - only Sam's own insistence on live verification caught it.
Fixed (commit 952b338) by giving `.ph img` the same `position:absolute;inset:0` treatment `.ph .none`
already had. This is the shared base `.ph`/`.ph img` rule, so the fix also covers every other real-
photo card using the same aspect-ratio'd `.ph` (grid2/grid3/cards5 - class_era/refusal/VIN-confirm,
out of this round's own scope but carrying the identical bug before this fix). Re-verified live after
redeploy: all three card photos on the CLK DTM page now measure 320x213.33, bit-identical.

LIVE VERIFICATION (goasksam.com, real data, via the same `x-ops-key`/`x-launch-stage-test` header
technique `pushCheck.mjs` itself uses, `PROBE_KEY` read from the Keychain into one command's
environment, never printed): all four named cars and the mileage flow confirmed live, with real
data (not fixtures) - including a live "Live right now" table (five live 911s, "One is bidding below
the range, two above it.") and a real trimQuestion-driven identity line ("Which 911? Carrera S (8)
Carrera T (15)") I had no fixture for. Every font size matched the spec table exactly at both widths
on every page (72/48 range, 40/30 car name, 28/24 section heading, 24/20 card price, 17/16 scope,

  JOB 1, identity counts and bodies on bare year-and-model queries.
    (a) never nothing: the "1965 Ford Mustang" not_tracked Lane A saw was a failed archive read (a Supabase timeout or throttle leaves fetchQualifying with no rows and diag.queryError set; the engine then read the empty pool as "We haven't tracked a ... sale yet"). Now an empty pool with a failed read returns tier "read_failed" (samLine "The archive read did not finish. Try the search again in a moment."), mapEngineAnswer gives answerType zero_result with reasonFlag engine_read_failed, and answerCacheable never stores it. A bare year and model that resolves therefore returns a pool, an identity question, not_tracked only when the read completed and found nothing, or read_failed. (On the live archive "1965 Ford Mustang" reads 69 sales.)
    (b) the count on an option is the poolSize of the page it opens: the body refine (refine.body) now narrows the FINISHED pool (same rows, same window, same set-asides as the bare page) instead of filtering the rows before the window and outlier pass, and each option's n is computed by running buildPool with that refine on the same inputs. Output check (vii) identity_options_sum_to_pool fails an answer whose options do not add up or whose option n differs from the rows it holds; the sweep's checkIdentityCounts (enginecheck, identitycounts=0 to skip) opens every option with refine.body and compares the opened poolSize to the option's count.
    (c) every body present with at least one sale is offered: options come from the listings' own title words (titleBodyOf; e41 also accepted a stored body the model's facts offered, e42 removed that after the M5 proof), rows with no body word are counted as bodyUnspecified (in Any, in no option), and the identity question carries options, unspecified and total. Fastback is its own body on cars built before 1990 (a 1965 Mustang 2+2 is not the notchback coupe) and reads coupe from 1990 on (Ford's word for the S550 coupe). The scope line names every body present ("1965 Mustang, convertibles, coupes and fastbacks").
    PROOF on e41 (obdiag rows=1, gate clean on every car): 1965 Ford Mustang 69 sales, $22,000 to $38,500, options Convertible 34, Coupe 21, Fastback 12, unspecified 2, total 69 (before: Convertible 33, Coupe 19, 17 sales in no option). 2005 Porsche 911 39: Coupe 24, Cabriolet 14, Targa 1, total 39. 1969 Chevrolet Camaro 21: Coupe 18, Convertible 3. 1995 Porsche 911 Carrera 37: Cabriolet 21, Coupe 16. 2018 Ford Mustang GT 8: Coupe 7, Convertible 1 (the 2018 "Fastback" titles read coupe). 1995 Acura NSX 15: Coupe 4, Convertible 2, unspecified 9.     FOR LANE A: raw answer fields on a result: `bodyOptions: [{ value: "coupe", label: "Coupe", n: 21, inPool: 21 }, ...]` (n = the poolSize the option opens with refine { body: value }; inPool = the rows of that body in this pool; equal by construction), `bodyUnspecified: 2`, `identityQuestion: { dimension: "body", prompt: "Which body style is it?", options: [{ label: "Convertible", n: 34, value: "convertible" }, { label: "Coupe", n: 21, value: "coupe" }, { label: "Fastback", n: 12, value: "fastback" }], unspecified: 2, total: 69 }`. Every option is offered (no eight-sale floor), so the identity line's Any count is `total`, which equals poolSize; a chip opens the SAME typed words with `refine: { body: value }` (never a re-query with the body word, which would run a different ladder). A new tier `read_failed` (raw) / answerType zero_result with reasonFlag "engine_read_failed" (mapped) means the read did not finish: show the "having trouble" line and a retry, never "We haven't tracked".
  JOB 2, the chosen body or trim comes back from the engine. On a refine the result's `resolvedCar` carries the applied choice: `resolvedCar.bodyStyle` is the chosen body ("coupe"), `resolvedCar.trim` is the chosen trim's name when a trim chip answered ("Carrera S"), and `resolvedCar.applied: { body: "coupe" | null, trim: "Carrera S" | null }` names what the refine applied. The scope label reads the choice like a typed word ("1965 Mustang Coupe", "2005 911 Carrera S, coupes and cabriolets"). FOR LANE A and FOR LANE C: read the car from `resolvedCar` (bodyStyle, trim, applied) after a choice, never from the chip label; Market Check, Buy, Sell and Tasks all see the same fields because they are on the one engine answer. Example (e42 proof below): "1965 Ford Mustang" with refine { body: "fastback" } -> resolvedCar { year: 1965, make: "Ford", model: "Mustang", trim: "", bodyStyle: "fastback", applied: { body: "fastback", trim: null } }, scope "1965 Mustang Fastback", poolSize 12.

## Lane B2, Oct 15 2026: resolver timeouts, Land Cruiser series, power-adder words, crew cookie in the checks

- Resolver lookups now time out. Every lookup in lib/vehicle.js (the taxonomy store reads, vPIC, OldCarsData /makes and /models, the VIN decoder) gives up after 4 seconds (RESOLVER_LOOKUP_MS) and takes the path an unreachable service already took, so the car resolves from the typed words and the curated data. After one timeout the rest of that burst skip straight to the fallback for 30 seconds, so a service that is down costs one timeout in total. Proof: scripts/resolverHangCheck.mjs (in prePush) makes every fetch hang forever and ignore the abort signal; the first resolve returns in about the timeout (4.04 s at the default, 1.5 s in the check) and the next ones in under 0.01 s. Before: one hung lookup held a resolve for 105 s. The longest resolve across the lanes check, with the network live: before 1.24 to 2.25 s over three runs, after 1.14 to 2.89 s over three runs (normal vPIC latency; the timeout changes nothing when lookups answer).
- Land Cruiser: "2012 Toyota Land Cruiser 200" read series 200 on ten of ten runs and under every failure mode I could simulate (offline, empty body, HTTP 500, slow, live), so the series read is deterministic; Lane C's one empty read was not reproduced (the one path not run here is the one with Supabase credentials). The series is now also read straight from the typed words, so it does not depend on which model name a lookup returned first.
- "Toyota Land Cruiser 80 Series" with no year: the year ask kept "Series" as a trim and dropped the 80. It now asks "Got it, a Toyota Land Cruiser 80. What year is it?" and the vehicle carries series 80. Also fixed: "Land Cruiser 80" and "Land Cruiser 60" read the number as the year 1980 and 1960 when the make was not typed; a number straight after Cruiser is the series now.
- Power-adder words: "Supercharged Dart 363-Powered 1965 Ford Mustang Fastback" resolved with trim "Supercharged Fastback", which has no market. A power-adder word (supercharged, turbocharged, twin turbo, blown, nitrous, stroked) the factory never sold on that make, model and year now leaves the trim and rides on the vehicle as `modifications` (kept through sanitizeResolvedVehicle). The title now resolves to the 1965 Mustang Fastback with modifications ["Supercharged"]; "1967 Chevrolet Camaro Supercharged" has no trim; where the factory sold the word it stays a trim (2013 Mustang Shelby GT500 Supercharged, 2016 Jaguar F-Type Supercharged, 2019 Challenger Hellcat Supercharged). The factory list is in lib/vehicle.js (FACTORY_POWER_ADDER): Jaguar, Land Rover, Lotus and Mini from 2002; Dodge, Jeep and Ram from 2015; Ford F-150 and Lightning from 1999; Mustang from 2003 only with a Cobra, GT500, Shelby or SVT trim; Chevrolet, Cadillac and GMC from 2004; Pontiac, Buick, Oldsmobile, Saturn and Mercury from 1989; Mercedes, Audi, Volkswagen, Toyota, Mazda and Maserati from 1989. A car outside the list reads as modified.
- FOR LANE B: the vehicle now carries `modifications` (an array of words, absent when none). The pool for the title is the model's own stock Fastbacks; if you want the answer to say that the typed words describe a modified car and that the sales shown are stock ones, read vehicle.modifications.
- scripts/pushCheck.mjs and the goldenTruth page reads mint the crew cookie from the Keychain item goasksam-crew (account goasksam) per run (scripts/_crewCookie.mjs): the code is held in memory to sign the cookie and is never printed, written, exported or placed in an address; without the item no cookie is sent. With the cookie the "catching his breath" failures are gone and the page timings are speed only.

## STANDING RULE FOR EVERY LANE: one archive load at a time (Sam, Oct 15 2026, from the speed job's stage 2 finding)
The slow Market Check and Buy reads measured on Oct 15 (08:30 to 10:10 PDT: uncached single reads 7 to 13s, up to 52s, against 3 to 5s overnight) overlapped no nightly job; they overlapped LANE WORK: prePush runs (each loads the 20 golden cars plus the perf reads), a cold-view test, a results table and an engine chain all in the same hour, and a live-Buy warm. The rule: no two lanes run prePush, a results table, a cold test or a chain at the same time, and no lane runs any of them while a live-Buy warm is on. Before starting one, say so in your lane's inbox message or here, and wait for the lane that is running one to report it finished. Lane B posts warm-start and warm-done in every lane's inbox; a warm runs at a width the minute probe (scripts/minuteProbe.mjs, one public read a minute) keeps at "ok" every minute, and drops its width the moment a minute reads unavailable (item 0 of the speed job). Stop only the processes you started yourself, by their own PIDs, never by process name; if you need another lane to stop something, write it here and tell Sam.

- 2026-10-15 (Lane B): THE ONE PREPUSH EXCEPTION (Sam, Oct 15 2026). e53 (0f46571) shipped a blank bare Market Check page for every car whose pool holds sales with no body word in the title (1965 Ford Mustang, 1969 Chevrolet Camaro): the new "Body not stated" option left the unspecified rows in bodyUnspecified as well, the output gate summed them twice (22 against a pool of 21), and the shared entry turned the answer into a cardless refusal; obdiag (runOneBox, no gate) still showed 21, which is how my proofs missed it. e54 (190d8ba) counts them once and makes a body page's refusal receipts its own rows. prePush against the live (e53) site failed on the identity-pages check and on the 1969 Camaro perf budgets (a cardless refusal cannot be warmed, so the Camaro page computed cold at 20s); Sam approved pushing e54 over those checks, this once, because the deployed site was the fault the push fixed. From here: prePush's identity check runs on the code being pushed (scripts/identityLocalCheck.mjs, synthetic rows through the real buildResult, options, option pages and gate, no network), the live-site check (scripts/identityPagesProof.mjs) runs in the post-deploy chain in its first minute, the sweep's Market Check lane reads through oneEngineAnswer (the gated entry), and nothing is ever again pushed over a failing prePush.

## Lane E, Buy speed: MEASURED (Oct 16 2026, 17:17 to 17:40 UTC), proposal below
Method, read-only, zero OldCarsData, one search at a time: scripts/buyTimes.mjs (new, Lane E) times the four searches
through the public endpoints from a real Chrome page (probe key + stage header, raw fetch gets the Vercel challenge):
ping (converse with no messages: the function round trip), parse (the resolver), chat (the real Buy turn with debug,
reading the stream: "text" marks the end of the model turn, "done" the end of enrichFast, which is the header + first
cards), explain (runSearch alone: resolver + live_listings read + fences), rerun (toolSearchLive + enrichFast, no model),
enrich (ten cards, blocking). `--page` runs the page itself the way pushCheck measures it (crew cookie, header and first
card off the DOM) and logs every request the page makes. scripts/buyProbe.mjs: one keyed POST for one-off reads.

WHERE THE TIME GOES (five samples each on a quiet archive, warm stored rows, before the e58 deploy; medians, seconds):
  step                                      | P911  | 65 Mustang | 2005 911 | 2023 GT3 | parallel? / cached?
  function round trip (ping)                | 0.13  | 0.11       | 0.12     | 0.12     | fixed cost
  resolver (parse)                          | 0.13  | 0.13       | 0.18     | 0.15     | already parallel with chat on the page; 1.9 s on a cold instance
  live_listings read + fences (explain)     | 0.7   | 0.6        | 0.6      | 0.6      | explain minus parse; could overlap the model's first round (it does not today)
  toolSearchLive total (rerun minus shape)  | 0.7   | 0.7        | 0.8      | 1.4      | nearest-years reads live_listings a second time (GT3); widen offers rerun on the rows read
  model turn (text minus tool)              | 4.1   | 5.1        | 5.3      | 4.6      | 2 or 3 Claude calls, each sequential: forced tool call (~1.5 s), the reply (~2 to 3 s), a guard regeneration (~1.5 to 2 s) on 7 of 12 samples here and 196 of 1,100 real turns in 14 days
  enrichFast (done minus text), 24/5/2/2 cards | 1.0 | 0.6        | 0.6      | 0.5      | 3 to 5 reads per card, all cards in parallel (24 for the 911: ~100 PostgREST requests at once)
  chat total to "done" (API)                | 6.3   | 6.2        | 6.7      | 6.5      |
  page: header = first card (pushCheck way) | 8.1   | 7.7        | 6.9      | 8.0      | the chat starts 0.35 s into the load; alerts_ready, watch ready, parse, track run beside it and cost nothing
  Market Check row (familyMarket) warm      | ~0.1 (one spec_market_cache read, inside explain; only year searches call it, via liveYearWindow)

THE SPIKES (the 13.6 s and worse): the steady state is 6 to 8 s and the model turn is most of it; the long waits are
all in the SAME turn under a cold or invalidated card cache, and I caught three:
  1. page run, Porsche 911: 18.5 s; page run, 2005 Porsche 911: 24.4 s (the "still finding" line showed at 20.4 s).
  2. API, Porsche 911 run 2 of measure2: model turn 3.1 s (2 calls), then enrichFast 7.5 s with ZERO pending cards.
     That is timelineOf -> asideRowsFor -> engineAnswer: a LIVE engine run on the request path for the first card
     with a sold appearance whose spec this instance got from the TABLE (specCore/prefetchSpecs fill specMem only,
     never rangeCache, so the set-aside check always misses rangeCache and computes a full pool).
  3. API, Porsche 911 right after the e58 deploy (every stored row invalid by engine version): turn 9.4 s, then
     enrichFast 15.8 s = 25.2 s total; 22 of 24 cards "pending"; each pending card's noBlock read fired a background
     refreshSpec (22 engine runs through 8 slots) and the one blocking set-aside engine read queued behind them. A
     blocking enrich of the same 24 ids then took 161 s with 9 still pending. The same state recurs every day at
     00:00 UTC (prefetchSpecs rejects rows from an earlier UTC day: sameUtcDay) until the nightly job rebuilds, and
     after any ENGINE_VERSION bump until the warm finishes.
  4. One turn of 20 hit the 25 s deadline (2005 Porsche 911, no text, no trace in the done event): with the deadline
     the done event carries no stage times, so model stall vs tool stall cannot be told apart from outside.
  Also seen: prefetchSpecs treats a FAILED table read (null) as "the table has nothing" and marks every key in the
  batch missing for two minutes (specMiss), so one throttled read turns a whole result into pending cards and a
  background recompute of every spec.

PROPOSAL (smallest change per slow step; every sales pool, fence and range untouched; each one reversible alone):
  E1  Search turn, no regeneration call (samChat.js + chatCore.js, ~1.5 to 2 s on ~18% of turns). The page already
      strips the model's search-turn reply to the one surviving sentence (cleanSearchReply) and shows the box; the
      guard today regenerates on wording the page then throws away ("a choice question", "more than one question").
      Change: on a search turn the reply is cleaned BEFORE the guard (chatCore passes the reply to surface.override;
      BUY.override returns cleanSearchReply(reply) or the code reply "Here they are."); the guard still checks what
      survives. The page text is identical to today's.
  E2  One stored-row read for all shown cards instead of one per card (samChat.js, ~24 parallel PostgREST reads -> 1
      for Porsche 911): toolSearchLive resolves the shown cards' specs, calls prefetchSpecs(keys) once, then the
      per-card listingMarket(noBlock) hits memory. Same rows, same answers.
  E3  Start the cards' enrichment when the search tool returns, in parallel with the model's reply round, instead of
      after it (chatHttp.js passes an optional prepare hook; toolSearchLive starts it; buyChat's shape awaits it).
      Saves the whole enrichFast (0.5 to 1 s warm, the full spike under a cold cache) off the critical path. Needs a
      two-line change in api/buySearch.js (FOR LANE C below); inert until that lands.
  E4  The set-aside label must not run the engine on the request path (FOR LANE C, api/buySearch.js timelineOf, with
      lib/tasks/setAside.js asideRowsFor): bound the engine wait (Promise.race, 1500 ms); past it the timeline draws
      without the label and the page's own 20 s enrich retry fills it (the engine run keeps going in the background,
      inflight, so the retry finds it). Labels only; no pool, fence or range. This is the 7.5 s and the 15.8 s.
  E5  FOR LANE B (lib/live/search.js prefetchSpecs): a null (failed) table read must not mark the batch's keys as
      missing for two minutes. Diff: inside the `for (let i = 0; ...)` loop, after
        const rows = await supabaseSelect(...).catch(() => null);
      add
        if (rows == null) continue;   // a read that failed is not a table with nothing in it: ask again next time
      Behaviour: a throttled read no longer turns every card pending and no longer fires a background engine run per
      card; the next card ask reads the table again.
  E6  SAM'S DECISION: YES (Oct 16 2026), IMPLEMENTED (see the READY line): skip the model's reply round on a search turn entirely (the tool call is the
      only round; the reply is "Here they are." in code). Saves 2 to 3 s on EVERY search (the model turn would be the
      forced tool call alone, ~1.5 s). Cost: the occasional surviving model sentence above the cards ("Two of the five
      are ending today, including a red coupe...") would no longer appear; the counts, chips, nearest-years line and
      widen offers are all built in code already and unaffected.
  E7  Noted for Lane B, not mine: the 00:00 UTC row reset (sameUtcDay) and each ENGINE_VERSION bump put Buy into the
      spike state until the warm finishes; engineGenerations costs up to 3 s per model-only search on a cold instance.
  Debug only: the chat's done event, with debug, also carries stage times (tool ms per call, model ms per round,
  shape ms), and the deadline path keeps them, so the next spike can be read without a script.

## The crew cookie: lifetime, what ends it, and the gated pages (Lane C, 2026-10-16, for Sam and every lane; no cookie value here)
HOW IT WORKS (lib/_crew.js, api/crew.js on main): gas_crew = v1.<expiry ms>.<HMAC-SHA256 over "gas_crew|v1|<expiry>">, keyed from CURTAIN_CREW_CODE. Minted only by /api/crew?code=<CURTAIN_CREW_CODE> (the crew link), Set-Cookie Max-Age 31536000 (one year), Path=/, Domain=goasksam.com (so www and every subdomain; a cookie minted on a *.vercel.app address is host-only and never reaches goasksam.com), SameSite=Lax, Secure, not HttpOnly. Nothing is stored on the server: every check recomputes the signature (isCrewRequest).
LIFETIME: one year from the moment it is minted. The cookie Sam stored today expires 2027-10-14. Not short; no change proposed.
WHAT ENDS IT, and nothing else: (1) its expiry passing; (2) CURTAIN_CREW_CODE changed in Vercel (every crew cookie ends at once; the env listing shows the variable created 52 days ago, Production only, and a cookie minted earlier still verifies now, so it has not changed since then); (3) CURTAIN_CREW_CODE unset (nothing is crew, fail closed); (4) the browser losing it (cleared site data, a private window, a different browser profile). A deploy does NOT end it (the signature depends only on the secret), and a sign-in or sign-out elsewhere does NOT (no code on main writes or clears gas_crew; the only page scripts that write cookies set gas_consent and clear gas_free_used).
THE GATED PAGES honour one cookie the same way (checked live just now, one load each, real browser): with the cookie, /partner-demo, /market-check, /business, /buy and /tasks all answer 200 and stay on their page; without it, /partner-demo is a plain 404 and the other four 302 to /sell. Every one of them goes through the same isCrewRequest (Business via isReleased, which calls it first). The demo is reachable for crew.
WHY LANE A'S COOKIE WAS REFUSED (its note above, item 1): a 302 to /sell means the request reached the page and isCrewRequest said no. With the secret unchanged and the same cookie working on every page, the cookie itself did not verify: a value minted from a local copy of the secret that does not match production's, the old plain value, or an expired one. Not a deploy and not a page difference. A DIFFERENT symptom to keep apart: a plain Node or curl request now gets Vercel's bot-challenge 429 whatever its cookie (seen today on /business, /partner-demo and /api/sellerDecision); that is not a cookie refusal, and it is why Lane C's live checks run in a real browser.
FOR EVERY LANE: never mint a crew cookie locally. Read the one Sam stored, at run time, from the Keychain (service goasksam-crew, account goasksam), never printed or written anywhere; set it on goasksam.com only; send requests from a real browser page. If a lane's cookie is refused, check its v1.<expiry> date first, then ask Sam for a fresh crew link in his own browser; do not ask anyone to paste a cookie.

## Partner demo access code, stage 1: built (Lane C, 2026-10-16; commit 1c536749, local, not pushed)
Entry: /partner-demo?k=<the code> (also ?code=). The value is compared with PARTNER_DEMO_CODE in constant time. On a match the page sets gas_partner and answers 302 to /partner-demo with no query string. A wrong, empty or missing code, too many attempts from one address (lib/_ceilings.js partner_code: 5 a minute, 20 an hour, 50 a day per address and per device), or no PARTNER_DEMO_CODE set at all, gets the same plain 404 a visitor gets today, with no redirect, no cookie and no hint that a code exists.
Cookie: gas_partner = p1.<expiry>.<HMAC-SHA256>, signed with a key derived from PARTNER_DEMO_CODE (never the crew key), HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days (Sam's own message said 14; Lane F's relay said 30, Sam to say if 30 is wanted), host-only, set twice: Path=/partner-demo and Path=/api/partnerAnswer, so the browser sends it to those two paths only. Changing PARTNER_DEMO_CODE in Vercel ends every gas_partner cookie; rotating CURTAIN_CREW_CODE does not touch them.
Scope: only api/partnerDemo.js and api/partnerAnswer.js read gas_partner, and it never counts as crew, so every crew-gated page refuses it: /market-check, /business, /buy, /sell, /tasks and /tasks/mine, /desk, /onebox, /how-sam-decides crew view, the VIN, history and spec crew views. The crew cookie still opens the demo and its data endpoint. The demo's hero image moved under /partner-demo (?img=hero) so it rides the same path-scoped cookie.
Headers on every demo answer (200, 302 and 404): Cache-Control private, no-store; X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow; Referrer-Policy no-referrer. Still linked from nowhere. The engine is untouched: every figure still comes from Market Check's own handler (partnerEngineMatch offline 32 of 32).
Test: scripts/partnerAccessCheck.mjs, now in prePush, runs the real handlers with made-up codes generated in the run (no real value anywhere): 30 passed, 0 failed (the right code by ?k= and ?code=; the redirect carries no query and no header carries the code; both cookie paths and flags; the page, the hero and the data endpoint open with gas_partner; gas_partner is never crew; only the two demo files read it; wrong, empty, empty ?code= and one-character-off codes give the visitor's 404 with no cookie; the per-address limit exists; the headers; the crew cookie still opens both; rotating the crew code leaves gas_partner working; changing PARTNER_DEMO_CODE ends it; an expired or made-up cookie is refused; with no PARTNER_DEMO_CODE nothing opens).
Note: Vercel's own request log records the address a browser asked for, so the first request's ?k= appears there once (Vercel logs are private to the project); the page itself never echoes, logs or stores it, and the redirect clears it from the address bar and from any Referer.
Next: prePush alone once, push in the next batch (demo first), then the live checks. Sam sets PARTNER_DEMO_CODE when the PUSHED line says so.

## Partner demo shows no sales: the cause (Lane C, 2026-10-17 ~00:10Z, before any fix)
Cause (b), from Lane C's access-code push (ba6560b5), not a cold read. The data endpoint (api/partnerAnswer.js) gets every figure by calling Market Check's own handler (api/sellerDecision.js) in-process, passing the visitor's own headers. Market Check is still sealed before launch: lines 2836 to 2849 refuse a request that is not crew, not a tester and not an internal warm (CURTAIN_SEALED), and refuse the oneBox read when Market Check is not released for the request (isReleased). A browser that opened the demo with the code holds gas_partner and no crew cookie, so the in-process Market Check read was refused, partnerShape got no one_box answer, and the page drew "Sam could not read the sales just now"; view d's sales section then fell to its empty text, "No recorded sales of cars like this yet.", which is false for a car with 43 sales (Lane C's page bug, fixed in the next push). A non-crew caller would also count against Market Check's per-visitor daily car limit. Lane C's own live checks used the crew cookie, which Market Check honours, so they passed and missed this.
Per car, data endpoint from a real browser with the crew cookie, one read each (00:05Z): 2015 Porsche 911 GT3 200, 1.3 s, range, 43 sales; 2005 Porsche 911 200, 4.0 s, range, 38; 1965 Ford Mustang 200, 2.7 s, range, 69; 1957 Porsche 356 Speedster 200, 1.0 s, range, 8; 1966 Ferrari 275 GTB 200, 0.9 s, not enough for a range, 9; 2023 Porsche 911 GT3 200, 1.1 s, range, 9. All answers fast, so no cold-read overrun.
View c drew the grey placeholder because its listing mock was kept on purpose (hero on b and d only, per the earlier brief); Sam now wants the hero on c too.
FIX (building now): (1) the endpoint's in-process Market Check read carries the server's own internal credential from the environment (never sent anywhere, never printed), so a partner session reads exactly what crew reads; the partner gate and the partner_answer ceiling stay in front of it; no engine change, the same oneEngineAnswer path. FOR LANE B: a proper internal-caller flag in sellerDecision.js would be cleaner than borrowing the test path; Lane C uses the existing credential until then. (2) A failed or timed-out read never prints the no-sales text; it retries once after a few seconds, then prints the could-not-read line. (3) The endpoint keeps the last good answer per demo car verbatim with its readAt and shows it only if a live read fails and it is under a day old. (4) View c gets the hero in its main slot and thumbnails.

  rows) THEN taxonomy_aliases (5,000 rows), then getModelsForMake reads the make's models, then getVpicModelsForMakeYear
  calls vPIC, all in series on the request path. TAXONOMY_CACHE_TTL_MS is 10 minutes, so every instance reloads the whole
  taxonomy on the request path every 10 minutes even when warm: on a quiet archive a cold parse was 1.9 s against 0.13 s
  warm; under archive load the page's own parse took 7.8 s (the 1965 Mustang run at 19:41Z). A make+year the instance has
  not seen cost 0.45 to 0.77 s on production (three rare pairs; the vPIC call is quick from Vercel's region, 1.2 to 5.2 s

  seed runs) with a background refresh (serve the cached copy, refresh past TTL in the background, never on the request
  path); (b) makes, aliases and the make's models read in parallel (Promise.all) and vPIC alongside, not after; (c) a

## Lane E, SEO and AI-search AUDIT (read-only, Oct 16 2026, 22:10 to 22:40Z; nothing public changed)
Method: scripts/seoAudit.mjs (branch seo-audit) fetches each URL as a crawler does (Googlebot user agent, no JavaScript,
no cookies, redirects not followed) and reads the raw HTML; a second pass with the automation bypass reads the pages the
edge challenges. Firewall config read through the Vercel API (read-only). Times are one crawler fetch, uncached.

HOW A CRAWLER IS TREATED AT THE EDGE (the first finding, Sam's decision): Vercel's Bot Protection managed rule is ON with
action "challenge" (since Aug 26 2026) and one custom bypass rule lists exactly: /, /sell, /about, /how-sam-decides,
/powersellers, /privacy, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /onebox, /onebox-preview, /api/signup and the asset prefixes. Every
other public URL answers HTTP 429 + x-vercel-mitigated: challenge to a crawler Vercel cannot verify by IP: the sitemap
INDEX that robots.txt points to (/sitemap-index.xml), every dynamic sitemap (-pages, -specs, -vins*, -motorcycles,
-other, -hubs), every /history page, every /cars page, /mcp, /buy, /market-check, /tasks, /business, /llms.txt. Verified
search crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) pass Bot Protection by Vercel's IP verification; an AI answer engine's fetcher, a link

(sales 3.1 s, attempts 1.9 s, in parallel), resolve 0.05 s, onebox 2 ms (a stored row), render 2 ms, total 3.2 s; year hub
/history/1965-ford-mustang = hubvins 0.36 s (the "340 ms family list"), resolve 0.27 s, onebox 14.7 s (a LIVE engine run,
no stored row), total 15.4 s; the car page /history/1965-ford-mustang/5F08C607450 = 15.3 s (the same engine run plus the
200-row family list), the BMW car page 2.2 s (a stored row). Every one of these renders on every fetch: the handler's
Cache-Control is "public, s-maxage=30" ONLY when fullyLaunched() (stage 2 + LAUNCH_BUSINESS=1) and the request carries no
crew cookie or credential; today that is "private, no-store" for every visitor and crawler on every SSR page (history,
spec, sell, how-sam-decides, business, buy, tasks, market-check). A Vercel deployment purges the edge cache, and a launch
stage change needs a redeploy to take effect, so the fullyLaunched() gate buys no safety that the deploy does not already
give. SHOULD THE PAGE BE CACHED: yes. Proposed: hubs and car pages "public, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=86400"
for anonymous requests (the nightly ingest changes them once a day; crew and credentialed requests stay private), and no
live engine run on a crawl (below). Cost today per crawl of the 20,000 VIN pages at 2 to 15 s each is the archive's whole
day; cached, the first fetch pays and the rest are free.

  # GoAskSam
  > Where collector cars actually sell: real auction results, one car at a time, as of October 2026.
  GoAskSam answers three questions from recorded auction sales: what a collector car has sold for, the full auction
  history of one car by its VIN, and where a car like it is most likely to sell well. Every figure on the site comes
  from a recorded sale. There are no appraisals and no guesses; when the record is thin, the page says so.
  ## Pages
  - Where to sell: https://goasksam.com/sell
  - What a model has sold for (Porsche 911 first): https://goasksam.com/cars/porsche/911
  - Every car by VIN, with each car's own auction history: https://goasksam.com/history/porsche-911
  - How Sam decides (the method, written plainly): https://goasksam.com/how-sam-decides
  - GoAskSam in ChatGPT and Claude (the MCP server): https://goasksam.com/mcp
  - About: https://goasksam.com/about
  ## Sitemaps
  - https://goasksam.com/sitemap.xml
  ## Terms of use for answer engines
  - Quote a page's dated lead sentence and link the page; the date on each page is the date of the record it was built from.
  - A car page describes one car by VIN; a model page describes recorded sales of that model in the last twelve months.
  - "Sam" is the name of the service's voice, not a person.

```
# GoAskSam

> Where collector cars actually sell. Real auction results, one car at a time.

GoAskSam answers three questions from recorded auction sales: what a collector car has sold for, the full auction history of one car by its VIN, and where a car like it is most likely to sell well. Every figure on the site comes from a recorded sale. There are no appraisals and no guesses. When the record is thin, the page says so.

Go ask Sam is the brand's call to action. Sam is the name of the service, the voice that answers.

## Pages

* Where to sell: https://goasksam.com/sell
* What a model has sold for, Porsche 911 first: https://goasksam.com/cars/porsche/911
* Every car by VIN, each with its own auction history: https://goasksam.com/history/porsche-911
* How Sam decides, the method in plain words: https://goasksam.com/how-sam-decides
* GoAskSam inside assistants that support the Model Context Protocol: https://goasksam.com/mcp
* About: https://goasksam.com/about

## Sitemaps

* https://goasksam.com/sitemap.xml

## For answer engines

* Quote a page's opening sentence and link the page. Each page states the date of the record it was built from.
* A car page describes one car by VIN. A model page describes recorded sales of that model.
* Sam is the name of the service, not a person.
```

## The 13.5 MB watch-event read: proposal before building (Lane C, 2026-10-17; Lane D's observation, Sam: not a launch blocker)
WHAT HAPPENS: a spec watch's events come from lib/live/watches.js specEvents, which asks cohortAnswer, which asks lib/live/search.js engineAnswer. engineAnswer checks only this instance's memory (rangeCache) and an in-flight read, then runs the whole engine (oneEngineAnswer) against the archive. It writes the result as the stored Market Check answer for that spec, but never READS that stored answer first. So on every cold instance the quarter-hour send cron recomputes every watched spec from the archive: Lane D measured 13,528,841 bytes for three watches on the first run, under 10 KB on every later run of the same instance. It grows with every watch.
WHAT A WATCH USES from the answer: cards (the qualifying sales, price and date), setAsideRows (with reasons), cluster (today's range), bodyScoped and fallbackRung, and rawPool for ONE thing: bandBefore, the range as it stood in the twelve months before each new sale. rawPool and cards are the same qualifying rows (lib/onebox.js: cards = shapeCards(solid), rawPool = solid), with the same price (r._usd = card.price) and date (auction_end_date = card.date).
PROPOSAL, the narrowest fix, in Lane C's file only (lib/live/watches.js), no engine change:
  1. bandBefore reads d.cards (price, date) instead of d.rawPool: the same rows and the same r4Cluster call, so every band is unchanged, and the watch no longer needs the raw pool.
  2. cohortAnswer reads the spec's STORED Market Check answer first (the same row engineAnswer writes, under the same specKeyFor key, the row Market Check serves) and runs the live engine only when no stored row exists. A stored row from yesterday (stale) is still used: a watch reports sales newer than its baseline, and a sale the stale row has not yet absorbed is reported on the next run after the row recomputes (the stale recompute runs on the next visit to that spec).
  Expected: a cold send run reads one stored row per watch (a few KB each) instead of the whole pool; no figure or band changes.
NEEDS FROM LANE B before building: (a) confirm the stored Market Check row keeps cards, setAsideRows, cluster, bodyScoped and fallbackRung intact (the e59 egress job slimmed the Market Check RESPONSE; is the STORED row slimmed too?); (b) the read call for a stored row by specKeyFor key that Lane B wants used (lib/live/search.js is Lane B's file, so Lane C would call Lane B's reader, not write a second one).
PROOF PLAN after building: a fixture through specEvents with rawPool removed gives the same events and the same bands as today; one dry send run on a cold instance with bytesRead before and after (Lane D's dry-run path, &dry=1), the before being Lane D's 13.5 MB.
